### TAG-198: Example 12.25 Pure Value Expression

**Status:** 🟡 Partial

## Software Notes

**I checked every symbol used here —** `K, L, M, N, S, T, U, V, W, X` — against the boundary ports `A, B, CI` and destinations `SUM, CO`, and none of them collide. This example is collision-free as printed. That's a real, meaningful difference from [TAG-177](https://linear.app/taguniversal/issue/TAG-177/example-1226-pure-value-expression-of-boolean-full-adder), and it means this one has a real shot at actually compiling and running correctly.

Two things worth working through before transcribing it, though.

### 1. Same comma-disambiguation gap as 12.26 — needs the same fix

The joint-match rules are written as bare concatenation (`SUW[K,M]`, `TVX[L,N]`) — same ambiguous form 12.26 originally had before we established the comma convention. These are all genuine 3-symbol joint matches (one dual-rail state each from A, B, and CI), so they need the same treatment:

```
S,U,W[K,M]   S,U,X[L,M]   S,V,W[L,M]   S,V,X[K,N]
T,U,W[L,M]   T,U,X[K,N]   T,V,W[K,N]   T,V,X[L,N]
```

I checked these by hand against the actual full-adder truth table before trusting them — `S,U,W` (A=0, B=0, CI=0) → `K,M` (SUM=0, CO=0) ✓, `T,V,X` (A=1, B=1, CI=1) → `L,N` (SUM=1, CO=1) ✓, and I traced the rest too — all eight rows are internally consistent with binary addition. This is structurally much simpler than 12.26 as well: one flat tier of eight 3-way joint matches computing the whole truth table directly, rather than 12.26's cascaded multi-tier gate derivation. That maps cleanly onto exactly the mechanism we already built — `collectValueTransformRules`/`groupRulesByTarget` doesn't care about arity, three-input joint matches work through the identical code path as `GI[S]`'s two-input ones.

### 2. A gap I want to flag explicitly, because it's not new — it's the *same* gap, twice now

Nothing in this rule list ever *produces* `S, T, U, V, W, X` — they only appear as joint-match *inputs*. The prose legend tells us what they mean ("S means A=0"), but that's a semantic description, not a rule. This is the identical shape of the problem I flagged for 12.26's `A–F` — and seeing it twice now makes me much more confident it isn't a one-off transcription gap in either example. I think it's very likely a **standard dual-rail-splitting pattern Fant establishes once, earlier in the chapter**, and then invokes by reference in every example from that point on without re-deriving it each time — the same way a programmer doesn't re-explain what `+` does in every function that uses it.

If that's right, there should be an earlier section — plausibly something in §12.7's "Expression Structure" territory ([TAG-52](https://linear.app/taguniversal/issue/TAG-52/127-expression-structure)), or wherever boundary-place dual-rail encoding first gets introduced — that shows the actual mechanism: how a boundary place holding a plain value asserts the two named symbols representing its 0/1 states. Do you have that section, or can you check? Without it, neither this example nor 12.26 can actually be simulated end-to-end — both are missing their own trigger, and I'd rather find the real pattern than invent a plausible-looking one and risk repeating exactly the mistake that cost us so much time on 12.26.

## Reference

### 12.8.7 Pure Value Expression

The values K, L, M, and N are added as output values that are unique from the input values.

* S means A = 0
* T means A = 1
* U means B = 0
* V means B = 1
* W means CI = 0
* X means CI = 1
* K means SUM = 0
* L means SUM = 1
* M means CO = 0
* N means CO = 1

The output values can now be delivered to the place of resolution as free values and can effect their own output, in this case by invoking a definition that contains a source place with themselves as content that associates to $SUM and$CARRY. The expression of Example 12.25, as a whole, is a pure value expression.

```
FULLADD($A,$B,$C)(< > CARRYOUT< >)
FULLADD[(A< > B< > CI< >)($SUM$CO)

$A$B$CI :
K[SUM<K>] L[SUM<L>] M[CO<M>] N[CO<N>]
S,U,W[K,M] S,U,X[L,M] S,V,W[L,M] S,V,X[K,N]
T,U,W[L,M] T,U,X[K,N] T,V,W[K,N] T,V,X[L,N] ]
```
